name: Sabey Data Centers Ashburn - Building C

source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Building C at Sabey's Ashburn campus publishes 54 MW of IT capacity. Across the 19 Virginia facilities on this site that have published a megawatt figure, the total is 1,326 MW, and Building C ranks sixth among them, accounting for roughly 4 percent of that published total. Virginia has 326 mapped facilities in this site's dataset, and the vast majority publish no capacity figure, so the true share of state capacity this building represents is unknown.

The 54 MW figure sets a ceiling on what the building can host for AI workloads. As an assumption, at 40 kW per rack, a density common for GPU training servers, 54 MW of IT load translates to roughly 1,350 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a more conservative colocation assumption, the same power supports roughly 5,400 racks. The operator publishes no rack count, no cooling architecture, and no power density per cabinet, so which end of that range is achievable here is not determinable from published data.

The certifications qualify the campus to host workloads subject to financial audit controls (SOC 1 Type 2), security and availability audit controls (SOC 2 Type 2), payment card data requirements (PCI DSS), regulated health information (HIPAA), and international information security management standards (ISO 27001), with SSAE 18 as the underlying attestation standard for the SOC reports. Those certifications make the facility eligible for regulated enterprise and government AI workloads, not only hyperscale training. Who actually occupies the building is not published.
